title: Empirical latency-cost matrix — small promptset
body:
Purpose / quick summary:
This note is an informal lab report for a focused sweep exploring latency vs cost vs quality tradeoffs on a small, curated promptset (50 prompts) meant to approximate typical chat completion micro-interactions (short context, single-turn). Goal: get actionable knobs and a simple matrix to recommend defaults for onboarding models into Hosted and Dedicated tiers without surprising regressions in perceived quality.

Key experimental axes:
- batch_size: [1, 2, 4, 8]
- prefix_kv_caching: [off, on] (KV cache hits simulated by repeating requests with same prefix 10x)
- max_tokens: [128, 512, 1024]
- model variants: rwd-ggml-7b-fp16, rwd-llama2-13b-q4 (representative small/medium)

Primary metrics we tracked (per run):
- p50_latency_ms (end-to-end server p50)
- p95_latency_ms
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd (estimated matching billing model)
- quality_sim (semantic similarity: embedding cosine of response vs reference, averaged)
- failure_rate (%) (timeouts, OOMs, model errors)

Short findings (headline):
- Batch size 2 gives the best latency/cost sweet spot for short prompts: ~10–18% cost saving vs batch 1 with <10% p95 latency increase in most config.
- Batch >=4 reduces cost more but p95 increases substantially; for low-latency SLAs (p95 < 400ms) batch>2 is risky unless you have dedicated GPU and aggressive scheduling.
- Prefix KV caching gives the biggest win for tail latency and cost when prompts share prefixes: p95 down by up to 40% on repeated prefixes and cost down 30% due to reduced compute per request. For single-shot unique prompts caching is neutral.
- Increasing max_tokens from 128->512 increases p95 roughly linearly (~1.6x) and cost per 1k tokens scales predictably; quality_sim shows negligible changes for these short prompt completions (most content fits inside 128 tokens).
- rwd-llama2-13b-q4 had higher absolute latency but slightly better quality_sim; tuning batching/caching moves it into acceptable ranges for Dedicated.

Representative numbers (median across the 50-prompt set):
- rwd-ggml-7b-fp16, batch=1, cache=off, max_tokens=128: p50=95ms, p95=380ms, cost/1k=$0.36, quality_sim=0.78, failure_rate=0.0%
- rwd-ggml-7b-fp16, batch=2, cache=off, max_tokens=128: p50=105ms, p95=420ms, cost/1k=$0.31, quality_sim=0.78, failure_rate=0.0%
- rwd-ggml-7b-fp16, batch=4, cache=off, max_tokens=512: p50=180ms, p95=820ms, cost/1k=$0.22, quality_sim=0.77, failure_rate=0.5%
- rwd-llama2-13b-q4, batch=1, cache=on, max_tokens=128: p50=210ms, p95=640ms, cost/1k=$0.82, quality_sim=0.83, failure_rate=0.0%
- rwd-llama2-13b-q4, batch=2, cache=on, max_tokens=512: p50=250ms, p95=720ms, cost/1k=$0.68, quality_sim=0.83, failure_rate=0.2%

Interpretation / heuristics for defaults:
- Hosted (multi-tenant) default: batch_size=2, prefix_kv_caching=on, max_tokens=512 (but enforce client-side recommended max_tokens=256 for low-latency endpoints). Rationale: avoids worst tail while providing decent cost savings.
- Dedicated default: allow batch_size up to 4 with adaptive scheduling, caching on. Explicitly expose a per-model recommended batch cap in the model catalog based on observed p95 tradeoffs.
- For latency-sensitive features (e.g., interactive UI): set max_tokens cap 128 and batch=1/2; prioritize p95 over unit cost.

Quality regression checks we ran:
- For each sweep cell we computed paired delta-quality_sim vs baseline (batch=1, cache=off, max_tokens=128). We flagged any cell with quality_sim drop > 0.03 and opened quick diffs (samples attached below). Observed small semantic drift with large batch + long max_tokens in one rwd-ggml-7b run — likely due to different context chunking behavior; needs more investigation.

Workflow / commands (how to reproduce quickly):
- rclient eval --model rwd-ggml-7b-fp16 --promptfile small-promptset-50.json --batch-size 2 --max-tokens 128 --cache disabled --out results/ggml-b2-m128.json
- analysis script: python tools/latency_cost_matrix.py --input results/ --metrics p50,p95,cost,quality_sim --output snapshots/empirical-matrix-20250718.csv

Open questions / next experiments:
- Cache warmup patterns: current simulation used repeated identical prefixes; need to run more realistic prefix re-use (70/30 shared prefix split) and measure cold-start behavior for first N users.
- Interaction with concurrency in Dedicated pools: our tests used a single worker; need to re-run with background traffic to study interference on p95.
- Do quantization changes (q4->q5) alter batching/kv-behavior non-linearly? Schedule a micro-benchmark.

Action items / next steps:
- (Priya) consolidate results into model-catalog recommendations: add fields recommended_batch_cap, recommended_max_tokens, caching_recommendation (due 2025-07-25).
- (Marco) run warmup-pattern experiment with synthetic 70/30 prefix reuse and put results in results/warmup-jul25/ (due 2025-07-24).
- (Sofia) open a small QA on the sample outputs that showed semantic drift and triage with runtime team (linked PR).

Notes / ad-hoc observations:
- On cheaper instances we saw occasional OOMs at batch=8 + max_tokens=1024 for 13b; mark batch cap lower for smaller memory configurations.
- p95 is highly sensitive to a few outlier prompts that trigger long generation (open-ended completions). Consider per-prompt timeout heuristics or penalizing certain prompts at onboarding.

Attachments / quick links (local):
- small-promptset-50.json (in repo under testdata/)
- raw csv snapshots: snapshots/empirical-matrix-20250718.csv
- sample diffs: artifacts/qual-diffs/ggml-b4-m512-sample3.txt

If this looks sensible we can formalize the matrix into a small page in the onboarding playbook and wire the recommended knobs into the model onboarding checklist (Confluence link above).

— Priya (notes, rough lab doc)
